target_customer: Young, tech-savvy Vietnamese retail investors, mostly aged 25 to 40
problem: Vietnamese consumers had little easy access to savings, funds and fixed-income products with low minimums; Infina fractionalizes them from about $25.
business_model: Retail investing platform earning distribution fees from asset managers and partners, with third-party super app integrations

founders.name: James Vuong
previous_startups: Reddit-style platform in Vietnam (acquired by LINE in 2017, per YC page)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch June 2021: engineer in Silicon Valley, VP of investment and Kauffman Fellow at IDG Ventures. Education not found.

competitors.name: Ajaib
competitors.funding_then: $65M Series A extension led by Ribbit Capital, round total $90M

competitors.name: StashAway
competitors.funding_then: $25M Series D led by Sequoia Capital India

technical_complexity.rationale: A consumer app integrating multiple licensed asset managers, payments and a securities partner, with compliance constraints in Vietnam, but standard engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Partner integrations, licences via partners and accumulated customer money create friction, but products are distributed by many apps.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action found; JB Financial Group bought a minority stake in March 2024.

market_need_then: Southeast Asian retail investing apps raised large rounds in 2021 and Infina reported 64% compound monthly growth in funded accounts in 2021 (TechCrunch, Feb 2022), indicating demand for low-minimum products.

branding.name_origin: CEO James Vuong said in a Vietcetera interview that he wanted a name that was less restrictive than RealStake and easier for Vietnamese speakers to say; where Infina itself came from is not stated.
branding.domain_note: Uses infina.vn and a .vn site; no acquisition details found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Personal, relatable stories about saving, with messaging on trust, flexibility and ease.

rebrands.why: Broaden offerings beyond fractional real estate and use a name easier for Vietnamese speakers; year approximate.

branding.community_and_virality: Distributed through third-party super apps including Tiki and partners like ZaloPay.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear Robinhood framing and local-friendly name, and the company claims over 4 million users across platforms (self-reported), but no independent brand press.

pivots.why: Broaden offerings, per the Vietcetera recap; exact date not stated.

outcome_analysis: Infina grew from a $2M seed in June 2021 to a $6M seed total in February 2022 backed by Surge, YC, Saison and others, then drew a strategic minority investment from JB Financial Group in March 2024. It claims over 4 million users across platforms through integrations with partners like Tiki and ZaloPay. No Series A was found, so growth appears capital-light and distribution-led.
notes: Founding year conflict: YC says 2021, CB Insights says 2018 (RealStake era). 2024 JB Financial amount and stake not stated; Caplight lists $12M total and ZoomInfo $6M, unverified. YC page cites Groww and Ajaib as comparables. The 2022 $4M extension is described as boosting the seed round to $6M; recorded as a separate seed tranche. Vuong's education not found.
